description:
## Goal

Resolve every callable reference exactly once through the ordinary lexical/expansion traversal, then retain its typed local or FunctionId identity through quote, macro execution, unquote, expansion, capture analysis, guards, and lowering. Source identifiers and qualified names exist only before resolution and for diagnostics or macro-visible display.

## Correct model

A module Namespace cannot identify local bindings. Local lexical identity is the pair of one typed SyntaxContext and the source identifier. The existing lowering environment and capture sets use that key as their single authority and map it to the existing ValueId; do not add a LocalBindingId registry, parallel environment, quote-only name set, scanner, or side table.

SyntaxContext is structural and immutable. A source body begins with its typed function/source owner. Each macro expansion extends its parent context with the exact macro FunctionId and structural syntax address of the invocation. Child addresses follow explicit AST edges and sequence positions, not scheduling order, allocation order, a global counter, heap address, display text, or source span alone. Equal reproduction yields the same context; repeated and nested invocations remain distinct. Canonical output renders the typed owner and structural path, never raw World allocation numbers.

Quote-introduced binders and references share the current expansion context. Unquote preserves the inserted caller context. Fresh dynamically constructed syntax acquires the insertion context exactly once. Existing branch, clause, block, pattern, and lambda scope rules decide visibility and rebinding; the context distinguishes concordant names owned by different syntax.

A callable target is either unresolved source carrying its exact Namespace, SyntaxContext, and validated source-name shape, or Bound(FunctionId). The single lexical traversal resolves a visible local through the contextual environment; otherwise a known definition-owned function becomes Bound and a missing name remains definition-owned. Definition-owned unresolved calls never inspect a caller context. Preserve the existing ordinary rule that macro classification precedes local callable dispatch.

Keep the standard quoted AST shape and encode typed context/target in existing metadata. Bound(FunctionId) is authoritative even if a macro changes the visible head spelling. Its display head is arbitrary quoted data: never expand, decode as source, or use it for dispatch. Creating a new semantic target requires fresh unresolved metadata, not a display-string edit. Argument changes validate bound arity and never choose another overload by spelling. Unresolved heads are validated as supported source-name shapes at the quoted read/decode boundary, so guard and lowering paths never rely on unreachable shape assumptions.

World remains the one identity and namespace authority. The owning QuotedSourceHeap carries one shared World identity-domain token inherited by roots and subroots; it does not retain World. Bind the heap when compiler-owned identities first enter it, preserve or validate the domain during cross-heap transport, and reject malformed or foreign typed identities before probing World. Do not serialize World identity into every node or introduce a resource, namespace snapshot, fallback resolver, binding store, or compatibility path.

## TDD signal

Use the cross-source macro case exposed during fz-tfn.53: App binds FutureMacros only as F, requires F.twice/1, and the provider macro quotes a call to its own double/1 helper. Prove both separate submission orders, driving only after the provider exists: each returns 42 and lowers the helper to the exact provider FunctionId. fz-tfn.46 owns the earlier requester-drive boundary, where today's unknown-import failure must become an observed exact ModuleInterface dependency and resume only when that provider arrives.

Prove all lexical ownership cases:

- A provider literal helper(41) ignores a same-spelled caller-local closure.
- A quote-introduced local = unquote(cb); local(41) selects that exact local.
- In the same expansion, unquote(caller_call) retains the caller's same-spelled local rather than the quote-local binding.
- A quote-local binding does not leak into the caller expression that follows the expansion.
- Repeated and nested invocations of the same macro cannot capture one another's locals.
- Generated lambdas capture exact contextual locals.
- Existing macro-before-local classification is unchanged.
- Missing provider names diagnose in the definition Namespace rather than borrowing caller locals.
- Fresh metadata resolves in its insertion context; copied metadata preserves ownership.

Also prove copied metadata and head-only edits preserve a bound target; argument edits cannot retarget overloads; malformed Unresolved heads diagnose in ordinary and guard paths; malformed, out-of-range, and foreign-World targets diagnose without panic; arbitrary Bound display heads remain inert; and typed targets survive interpreter/native tuple-map transport. Assert typed lowered targets/captures, not rendered names. Preserve macro inspection/composition, semantic equality, deterministic unchanged/unrelated zero work, and byte-identical artifacts across allocation noise.

## Strategy and deletion

Make the existing expansion/lexical traversal the one binding authority; it carries structural context while it already walks syntax and classifies macros. Generalize the existing environment and free-name/capture keys from String to the contextual lexical key, then delete downstream name-based local re-resolution and duplicate free-name authority. Collapse quote and ordinary call lowering onto the same typed target path.

Delete quoted_callable_name and every canonical module.function string used as post-resolution authority. Delete downstream generated-call module-path re-resolution and any workaround that adds provider names to caller namespaces or falls back from failed lexical lookup. Keep spelling and span only for unresolved source, diagnostics, and macro-visible display.

Update quoted-source and macro-expansion documentation to state the single-resolution, syntax-context, and metadata contracts. Full focused/library/fixture/CLI gates, formatting, check, strict Clippy, deterministic reuse proof, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review precede one commit and close. No temporary probe, duplicate traversal, compatibility path, or construction debris remains.
title: Keep callable identity through quoted source; delete canonical-name re-resolution
